title: Week 2 — Indicators of Sacred Law: The Qurʾān
subtitle: Sources · Dalīl · Qurʾān · Qaṭʿī vs Ẓannī
description: Explore the indicators of sacred law, their classification, and the Qurʾān as a legal source including the concepts of certainty and probability in transmission and indication.
source: Islamic Legal Theory I course material.

questions.q: A researcher is evaluating a legal indicator. According to the course, which three questions are central?
options: Who narrated it, when was it written, and who translated it?
Is it valid, is its indication probabilistic or non-probabilistic, and what major rules govern its use?
Is it Arabic, short, and widely known?
Does it concern worship, finance, or family law?

questions.q: Which set contains only indicators listed in the material as agreed upon by almost all jurists?
options: Qurʾān, Sunnah, congruent implicature, ijmāʿ, qiyās
Custom, istiḥsān, istiṣḥāb, maṣlaḥah mursalah, qiyās
Companion opinion, custom, Qurʾān, istiḥsān, sadd al-dharāʾiʿ
Pre-Islamic law, counter-implicature, custom, Sunnah, istiṣḥāb

questions.q: The entire Qurʾān is described as qaṭʿī from the perspective of narration because it is transmitted by:
Because the entire Qurʾān is qaṭʿī in transmission, every Qurʾānic verse must also be qaṭʿī in meaning.
Qurʾān 5:6 is discussed as an example of a phrase that may carry two meanings concerning “contact” with a woman. What does this illustrate?
options: Qaṭʿī al-thubūt and qaṭʿī al-dalālah in every respect

questions.q: The word “ten” in the instruction to feed ten poor people (Q. 5:89) is used as an example of:
options: A meaning open to several interpretations

questions.q: A command in the Qurʾān indicates obligation according to the predominant juristic view unless:
options: There is contextual evidence to the contrary
It appears in a long verse

questions.q: According to the predominant juristic view presented, a prohibition (nahy) indicates taḥrīm unless contextual evidence indicates otherwise.
A non-mutawātir reading attributed to a Companion is automatically considered part of the Qurʾān according to the material.
The material gives an example of Ibn Masʿūd’s reading adding the idea of fasting three days “consecutively.” Jurists debate whether such a reading can:
options: Serve as a valid indicator of sacred law rulings

questions.q: Which description correctly distinguishes ẓannī al-thubūt from ẓannī al-dalālah?
options: The first concerns transmission; the second concerns meaning/indication
The first concerns meaning; the second concerns the number of jurists
Both refer only to weak reports
Both mean that an indicator is invalid

questions.q: What are the two widely used English equivalents for dalīl mentioned in the material?
Name the two major legal-reasoning rules about commands and prohibitions discussed in the Qurʾān section.
acceptedAnswers: commands indicate obligation and prohibitions indicate forbidding unless contextual evidence indicates otherwise
amr indicates wujub and nahy indicates tahrim
amr means wujub; nahy means tahrim
questions.displayAnswer: An order indicates obligation (wujūb), and a prohibition indicates forbidding (taḥrīm), unless contextual evidence indicates otherwise.

questions.q: The material states that the Qurʾān is a valid indicator of sacred law rulings.
Which of the following is listed among the synonyms of “dalīl” in the material?
Which English equivalent of “dalīl” reflects traditional usage in books on uṣūl al-fiqh?
options: Neither is used in the field

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a debatable (not agreed upon) indicator?
How many debatable indicators of sacred law (al-adillah al-mukhtalaf fīhā) does the material list?
Which of the following is NOT one of the cases in which an indicator is probabilistic (ẓannī)?
options: It is narrated via āḥād reports
It may convey more than one meaning
It is both narrated via āḥād reports and may convey more than one meaning
It is narrated by tawātur and conveys only one meaning

questions.q: The Prophet’s statement that it is better to have a wash (ghusl) on Fridays (Sunan al-Tirmidhī) is used as an example of:
The report “There is no prayer when one does not recite al-Fātiḥah” (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī) is an example of an indicator that is:
options: Qaṭʿī in both narration and indication
Ẓannī in both narration and indication, since it is āḥād and “no prayer” may mean “no valid prayer” or “no complete prayer”

questions.q: According to the material, an indicator is qaṭʿī (non-probabilistic) if it is narrated by tawātur, or if it conveys only one meaning, or both.
The material says that how the Prophet performed prayers is transmitted by tawātur. It is therefore an example of an indicator that is:
options: Narrated only by a single narrator

questions.q: Which description matches the Qurʾān as defined in the material?
options: Human speech compiled by the Companions
God’s speech sent down to Prophet Muḥammad in Arabic, written in codices, recited as an act of worship, starting with al-Fātiḥah and ending with al-Nās, and transmitted by tawātur
Any report attributed to the Prophet
Any reading attributed to a Companion

questions.q: In the example of “contact” (Q. 4:43 / 5:6), how do jurists differ?
options: All agree it means only sexual contact
Some understand it as mere skin-to-skin contact, while others construe it as sexual contact
All agree it refers to menstruation
They disagree about the number of persons addressed

questions.q: Q. 2:43 commands the believers to establish the prayer. Under the predominant juristic view, this means that prayer is:
Q. 17:33 orders the believers not to kill others unlawfully. Under the predominant juristic view, this means that killing others is:
What is the term used in the material for a non-mutawātir (āḥād) reading of the Qurʾān?
According to the material, non-mutawātir (āḥād) readings by Companions may be considered part of the Qurʾān because Companions narrated them.
How do opponents respond to the argument based on Ibn Masʿūd’s reading “three consecutive days”?
options: They say Ibn Masʿūd was not a Companion

They say what he heard may have been an interpretation rather than a reading, it is not Prophetic Sunnah since he does not state he heard it from the Prophet, and it may be only a Companion’s personal opinion
They say the verse is qaṭʿī and cannot be interpreted
They say his reading is mutawātir but abrogated
